title: CV-Analyzer: desktop tool for evaluating cyclic voltammetry measurement series
description:
CV-Analyzer is a desktop tool for the evaluation of cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurement series: import of PalmSens (CSV and XLSX), Stanford Research Systems (SRS) and Raspberry Pi data as well as numpy arrays, splitting into cycles, Savitzky–Golay smoothing, point reduction by interpolation, potential correction against a reference electrode, integration of a potential window, peak fitting with Gaussian, Lorentz, Voigt and exponentially modified Gaussian shapes using particle swarm optimisation, and export of all results to Excel.

CV-Analyzer was written for the electrode characterisation work behind the publication “Voltammetric pH Determination and Water Quality Screening—A Novel Method Based on Iridium Dioxide Electrodes” and is the program required to open the .cvproj project files of the accompanying data set. It is not tied to a specific electrode system.

Requires Python 3.10 or newer; the peak fitting needs pygmo (PyPI on Linux, conda-forge on Windows and macOS). The user interface is in German. Project files use joblib/pickle serialization; the loader validates their content before unpickling, see the security note in the README.
